# Projective orbit attainment for a fixed positive fiber family

UPDATE 2026-09-18: `candidate 640d07cd1de2a423`
disproves the arbitrary-finite-base numerical target exactly. The
conditional orbit theorem below is not refuted; it may genuinely attain
a below-target minimum on three unequal sites. Its necessary conditions
therefore cannot imply the false numerical bound. Unweighted projective
orbits do not preserve the lattice-complete class required for OC.

This is a conditional extremal reduction for the stronger finite-base
target gamma_d/h(P). It is not a reduction that may be combined silently
with fixed-base shape stationarity. Its extra stationarity concerns
projective changes of the BASE. These maps generally do not preserve an
integer lattice, and this note uses them only in the stated finite-base
problem.

Fix d>=1. Let P be finite, affinely spanning E=R^r, and let K_p be positive
d-dimensional actual compatible convex fibers. Write S for their union,
mu for their unweighted fiber-volume measure, and h(P) for the Helly
number of the finite set P for convex-set traces. Put gamma=(d/(d+1))^d.
We assume in the attainment theorem that the finite-base depth bound
gamma/h(Q) holds for every finite base Q with fewer than |P| points and
every positive actual family over Q. Under a hypothetical failure of the
finite-base target, choosing the least possible number of base points
provides exactly this assumption. It is not assumed for P itself.

## 1. Positive affine weights are an exact geometric projective orbit

Translate E so that 0 is in the relative interior of conv(P). Let L be
affine and positive on P, hence positive throughout conv(P). Then
L(z)=b+a.z with b=L(0)>0. The full projective map

    F_L(z,x)=(z/L(z), x/L(z))                         (1)

is injective, convexity preserving, and has an inverse on its image chart.
Its base image P_L={p/L(p):p in P} has the same number of points. It maps
the convex hull of the original fibers to a convex body whose sections
at these specified points are exactly K_p/L(p). Every ambient closed
halfspace restricted to the source chart maps to an ambient closed
halfspace restricted to the image chart, up to the harmless whole-chart
or empty-chart cases.

The unweighted fiber-volume measure of the IMAGE body pulls back to

    dmu_L(p,x)=L(p)^(-d) dmu(p,x).                    (2)

This is the pullback of image GEOMETRIC volume. It is distinct from the
compensating L(p)^d weight for the pushforward of the ORIGINAL volume.
With (2), all point depths and their maximum are exactly preserved by
(1). Thus define D(L) to be maximum depth on the fixed candidate set S
with normalized measure mu_L; it is the genuine unweighted depth of
the projectively transformed actual family over P_L.

One also has h(P_L)=h(P). Here convex traces, rather than arbitrary
unbounded convex sets under a map with a restricted chart, give a simple
proof. A subset T of a finite set P is the trace of a convex set if and
only if P intersect conv(T)=T, with the empty case treated separately.
The forward direction follows from convexity; the reverse is realized
by conv(T). A positive projective map sends conv(T) exactly to
conv(F_L(T)), so it preserves the collection of all convex traces.
Minimal infeasible families of these traces, and hence their Helly
numbers, are identical.

## 2. Continuity without varying candidate points or halfspaces

Multiplying L by a positive constant does not change D(L). Normalize

    sum_(p in P) L(p)=|P|.

The admissible set A of strictly positive affine evaluation arrays has
compact closure

    Abar={affine evaluation arrays L>=0: sum L=|P|}.

Indeed it is a closed bounded subset of the finite-dimensional affine
evaluation space; affine spanning makes that evaluation map injective.

On A, D is continuous. For two normalized probability measures sigma,
tau on the SAME S, every cap mass differs by at most their total
variation distance. Taking the infimum at each fixed point and then
the maximum over the same candidate set yields

    |maxdepth(sigma)-maxdepth(tau)|<=||sigma-tau||_TV.  (3)

The finitely many normalized fiber density coefficients from (2) vary
continuously with L in A. Thus their measures converge in total
variation, proving the assertion. This does not interchange an infimum
with a merely weak measure limit, or move a candidate between fibers.

## 3. Boundary escape is controlled by a smaller actual base

Let L_j in A tend to L_infinity in Abar\A. The zero set

    F={p in P:L_infinity(p)=0}

is a nonempty proper exposed-face trace of P. It is proper because the
normalization excludes L_infinity identically zero. The original
fibers restricted to F form an actual positive family over F. For every
j their L_j-weighted measure is, by Section 1 applied within aff(F),
exactly the pullback of an unweighted projective actual family over
F_(L_j), with h(F_(L_j))=h(F).

Let M_j(F)=sum_(p in F) |K_p| L_j(p)^(-d), and similarly M_j(P).
All original fiber volumes are fixed and positive. Each term over F
tends to infinity, while the finitely many terms outside F remain
bounded. Therefore M_j(F)/M_j(P) tends to one. In the normalized whole
measure, a center in a retained F-fiber receives from every containing
halfspace at least its F-measure contribution. Consequently

    D(L_j)>= [M_j(F)/M_j(P)] D_F(L_j).               (4)

Here ambient and affine-span depth on F agree: a restricted halfspace
is a halfspace of aff(F) times R^d or a trivial whole/empty restriction,
and intrinsic halfspaces extend to the original ambient space. Thus
the smaller-base hypothesis gives D_F(L_j)>=gamma/h(F).

Finally h(F)<=h(P). To check this directly, every convex trace on the
exposed face F is also a convex trace on P: its convex hull lies in
that face and cannot acquire an off-face point of P. A minimal
infeasible family on F therefore gives an equally large minimal
infeasible family of traces on P. This proves the inequality.
Combining these facts gives the exact boundary estimate

    liminf_j D(L_j)>=gamma/h(F)>=gamma/h(P).          (5)

No classification of relative rates at which the several L_j(p) vanish
is needed. The smaller-base inequality applies at each j before any
limit is taken.

## 4. An attained projective minimum below the target

If D(1)<gamma/h(P), then inf_(L in A) D(L) is achieved at some
L_* in A and remains strictly below gamma/h(P).

Choose a minimizing sequence. Abar is compact. Any limiting point in
its boundary would contradict (5), since the infimum is at most
D(1)<gamma/h(P). Hence a subsequence limits to an interior admissible
L_*. Continuity from Section 2 shows that it attains the infimum.
After applying F_(L_*), the resulting bad actual family is stationary
under all sufficiently small projective base changes with positive
affine denominators. Composition of two such projective maps amounts
to another positive affine denominator in the original coordinates,
so this local stationarity follows from the attained orbit minimum.

## 5. Bulk base moments, including cap/facet coincidences

Work in the coordinates of such an attained orbit minimum, writing M for
its mass, beta for its maximum normalized depth, and Q=beta M. Choose
one positive critical cap circuit at each deepest fiber, and fixed
strictly cheaper circuit covers at the other fibers. Interior critical
centers and exact ambient cap circuits are supplied by the previously
proved cap-capacity construction. Write selected deepest caps as

    H_ij={a_ij.p+u_ij.x>=b_ij},  |u_ij|=1,
    sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0,  rho_ij>0, sum_j rho_ij=1.

Every cap of group i has mass Q and passes through an interior center
(p_i,x_i). Each circuit covers the whole fiber plane at p_i.

For a signed affine denominator perturbation L_t(p)=1+t A(p), the
measure density derivative on the fixed original fibers is -d A(p).
The derivative of a fixed cap mass is therefore

    B_ij(A)=-d integral_(H_ij) A(p) dmu.              (6)

Also allow affine cap motions, with margin velocity
ell_ij(p,x)=delta a_ij.p+delta u_ij.x-delta b_ij.
Require the linear equations

    sum_j rho_ij delta u_ij=0,
    sum_j rho_ij(delta a_ij.p_i-delta b_ij)=0.         (7)

These preserve the whole-fiber closed cover exactly at every selected
anchor. The signed affine A and the cap parameters satisfying (7)
form a finite-dimensional linear space D. Fixed nondeep covers remain
strictly below Q for small perturbations.

On a proper cap section the cap-motion derivative is integral ell_ij
with respect to H_(d-1). At a supporting facet with the body inside the
cap it is integral min(0,ell_ij); with the body outside the cap it is
integral max(ell_ij,0). Thus it is at most the supremum of the compact
convex set of linear forms

    g_ij=B_ij(A)+integral ell_ij dzeta_ij,            (8)

where zeta_ij is full area on proper sections and sigma times area on
coincident supporting facets, for any measurable sigma in [0,1]. The
same swept-slab argument used for the general boundary variation note
proves these branch formulas for arbitrary convex fibers; all changes
of density times newly swept volume are O(t^2). The own section is
proper with positive area, so every allowed S_ij=zeta_ij(total) is
strictly positive. No supporting-facet contribution is silently counted
as either a full proper section or a zero section.

Put L_0(A,delta caps)=-d integral A(p)dmu. Local projective minimality
implies that, as linear forms on D,

    L_0 belongs to cone(union_(i,j) G_ij),            (9)

where G_ij is the gradient set in (8). Here are the separation details.
The direction e with A=1 and all cap velocities zero has
L_0(e)=-d M and EVERY g_ij(e)=-d Q<0. Consequently a convergent sequence
in the cone in (9) has bounded total nonnegative coefficient, by
pairing with e. Compactness of the finitely many G_ij shows that this
cone is closed. If (9) failed, strict separation would give a direction
in D with L_0>0 and all g_ij<=0. Adding a sufficiently small positive
multiple of e keeps L_0>0 and makes all those inequalities strict.
The actual finite perturbation would then increase total mass while
putting every selected critical cap below the original budget Q.
The selected covers and the slack nondeep covers would bound the new
maximum normalized depth strictly below beta, contradicting the
attained orbit minimum. This proves (9).

Thus there exist lambda_ij>=0 and consistently chosen section measures
zeta_ij with L_0=sum lambda_ij g_ij on D. Testing on e gives

    sum_(i,j) lambda_ij=M/Q=1/beta.                  (10)

Testing signed affine A with all cap motions zero gives the exact
BULK base-moment identities

    integral A(p)dmu = sum_(i,j) lambda_ij
                                 integral_(H_ij) A(p)dmu.         (11)

This is one certificate for the whole selected collection and all
signed affine A. It is not a separate multiplier choice for each
coordinate. In particular it holds for the vector A(p)=p.

The coefficient structure can also be read without differentiating a
nonsmooth quantile. Pure threshold variations obey sum rho_ij delta
b_ij=0 within group i. Equation (9) then forces

    lambda_ij S_ij=c_i rho_ij,  c_i>=0.              (12)

Thus either every multiplier of a group is zero or all are positive.
Putting kappa_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/(sum_l rho_il/S_il) and
pi_i=beta sum_j lambda_ij gives pi_i>=0, sum pi_i=1, and
lambda_ij=pi_i kappa_ij/beta. The S_ij here are the CONSISTENT effective
section areas selected by the separation proof, including supporting
facet allocations. In the noncoincident case these are the ordinary
proper-cut areas and (12) agrees with the usual smooth quantile formula.

Every choice of one positive critical circuit at each deepest fiber
admits such a certificate. It can depend on the choice. All statements
retain arbitrary oblique caps, positive boundary-area coincidences,
and closed covers. The underlying fiber d-volume has no mass on a
nonvertical cap plane, so varying the density in (6) is unambiguous.

Moreover one may prescribe every INSIDE supporting-facet density sigma
in advance: min(0,ell)<=sigma ell for every sigma in[0,1]. Only the
outside densities then need vary in the gradient sets. The separation
and normalization are unchanged, so the bulk certificate exists for
EVERY such prescribed inside system, with possibly different multipliers.
See `candidate 9c6d3cb586898f7e`
for the corresponding exact local minimizing-cap inclusion.

## 6. The precise remaining restriction

Sections 1--4 prove an actual attained minimum on the projective orbit
of one FIXED positive family, conditional only on the smaller-base
target. Section 5 proves its bulk base-moment stationarity without
curvature or noncoincidence assumptions.

This orbit minimum has NOT been proved to be a local minimum with
respect to arbitrary body-shape changes over its transformed base.
Conversely, the earlier attained fixed-base shape minimum need not
be an orbit minimum after the base is allowed to move. It is invalid
to impose both sets of certificates, let alone identify their
multipliers, without a joint extremal theorem. No such theorem is
proved here. A simultaneous compactness argument has to control
correlated escape of denominators and shrinking original fibers;
the fixed positive-volume argument in Section 3 alone does not do so.
